draft.title: Agents of socialisation
card: Agents of socialisation are the people, groups and institutions that teach us how to behave and what to value. Their influence can be deliberate or unplanned.
usually the first agent. It teaches language, early habits and the values of the home.
peers are people of a similar age or standing, and they shape things like style, speech and interests. School teaches set subjects, and also rules, routines and how to work with others.
media, such as television, social media and news, spread ideas and images to many people. Religion can teach beliefs, moral values and customs.
draft.remember: Agents of socialisation are the sources that teach us how to behave and what to value.

a.q: Which example shows a peer group acting as an agent of socialisation?
opts: Friends in a sports team copy each other's slang and style
A teacher marks a class set of maths tests
A parent teaches a toddler to say thank you
A news website publishes an article on fuel prices
a.why: Friends of a similar age shape each other's speech and style, so this is peer influence. The parent example is tempting, but that is family teaching a child, not peers.
a.clue: Look for people of a similar age or standing influencing each other.

b.q: Priya moves to a new city. She watches online videos of local teens and starts to dress and speak like them, though no one has told her to. Which agent is mainly shaping her?
b.why: Her main source is online videos, which are media, and they spread styles and speech to many people. School is the tempting choice because the teens are local, but she is learning from videos, not from lessons or school rules.
b.clue: Where is she getting her ideas from, and is anyone teaching her in person?

a.best: Friends in a sports team copy each other's slang and style
